Walk into our shop and you get a Patriot Liner spray-on instead. Is the premium worth it? Here's what actually happens over time — and why we stopped carrying drop-ins years ago. How a Drop-In Bedliner Fails The fundamental problem with a plastic tray liner isn't what you can see — it's what's underneath it. Drop-ins don't seal to the truck bed. There's always a gap between the plastic and the metal, and that gap collects exactly what you don't want: rainwater, road salt, mud, and moisture. Over a typical Maryland winter: Salt-laden water gets under the liner and sits on bare metal The liner insulates it, keeping it damp longer than if the bed were exposed After 3–5 winters, you lift the liner and find rust that's been growing undetected Additionally, plastic hardens and becomes brittle in cold temperatures. Maryland winters regularly drop below 20°F — at those temperatures, drop-ins can crack when you drop cargo on them, and the plastic can warp enough to create even larger gaps at the edges. pages.body_excerpt: Capital Upfitters Team · April 2026 5 min read Maryland roads are salted aggressively every winter — over 200,000 tons of road salt distributed across state and county roads each season. That salt doesn't wash off cleanly. It gets packed into wheel wells, sprays up into frame rails, and settles into every exposed seam and crevice on the underside of your vehicle. Most truck and SUV owners don't think about undercoating until they see rust. By that point, it's already working against you. When Rust Actually Starts You don't see corrosion start — it happens in the places you never look. The first 3–5 Maryland winters cause surface oxidation on exposed metal: brake lines, frame rails, floor pan edges, and wheel well liners. After 5–8 winters without protection, surface rust deepens into pitting and structural compromise. The telltale signs you've waited too long: White powder (zinc oxide) building up in your wheel wells Brown or orange staining around the rear frame near the tow hitch Visible pitting or flaking on brake line brackets Bubbling paint on the rocker panels or door bottoms Once rust has pitted into the metal, undercoating seals over it — but it can't reverse it. The goal is to coat before corrosion establishes a foothold. The right window: August through October.
